text:
Roe v. Wade is controversial because it made a deeply contested moral question, when life or personhood begins and how to weigh it against a woman's bodily autonomy, into a nationwide constitutional rule. The majority found that the Fourteenth Amendment's protection of personal liberty includes a privacy right broad enough to cover the decision to end a pregnancy, which critics (including some legal scholars who support abortion rights) called weak reasoning and judicial overreach that cut off democratic debate. Supporters saw it as protecting reproductive freedom and health, so it stayed contested on both moral and constitutional grounds until Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization overturned it in 2022.
